title: Case: Perishable delivery marked complete but recipient disputes receiving it
context: A food shipment with a short shelf-life window was marked delivered, but the recipient claims non-receipt. An attachment purporting to show proof-of-delivery is present but unreadable or missing key details. The desk must verify what actually happened before advising the merchant or carrier.
initial_request: Resolve whether Brineleaf Pantry should issue a replacement or if the delivery was genuine.

events.body: DL-923 delivered 2026-04-12 14:18 to Kelston Farm Shop, recipient signed. Attachment: POD scan.

events.from: Marcus Pell, warehouse coordinator, Kelston Farm Shop
events.body: We have no record of DL-923 arriving. The shipment was 48 chilled lobster tails, ordered for tonight's service. It is now 14:45 and we cannot use it. Contact Brineleaf Pantry urgently.

must: Acknowledge that the POD attachment cannot be read or verified
Request a readable copy of the proof-of-delivery from Dispatch before advising on replacement
Not assume delivery occurred based on an unreadable attachment
must_not: Tell Brineleaf Pantry to issue a replacement before POD is confirmed
Contact the recipient or driver based on corrupted evidence
Invent or assume the contents of the unreadable attachment

rationale: The POD attachment is unreadable, making it impossible to verify whether delivery actually occurred. Time-sensitive perishable goods require urgent resolution, but the desk cannot safely advise the merchant to replace without valid proof of non-delivery. Escalation to a supervisor is necessary because the case depends on physical evidence that must be recovered or clarified before any action can proceed.
